written_by: hand, not by scripts/decoder-miri.sh; the record next to it is written by the script
not_covered: The memory-safety record is for zune-jpeg 0.5.16-rc3 (upstream commit c1c7f49). Nine of its fifteen integration test files did not finish in ten minutes each under the interpreter and are recorded as TIMEOUT; one unit test compares the integer addresses of two function pointers. It passes in a native debug build and fails in a native release build as well as under the interpreter, because the compiler may emit the same closure's code more than once; it is a fragile test and says nothing about memory safety. The native runs on aarch64 are in the pull request.
The aarch64 NEON code: Miri aborts on the intrinsics it uses (the failed runs in miri-record.json carry the error).
The AVX2 code on Miri's default target features: Miri reports no AVX2 unless it is compiled in, so the runs force it on; the 'upstream-x86-default' run passes without touching that code.
Inputs the fuzzer finds: Miri ran the crate's tests and the small seeds only, and is far too slow to follow a fuzz run.
Unsafe code in zune-core, flate2 and crc32fast, and whether those compile into the worker.
